_note: Held-constant configuration for the v1.1.0 SciBench campaign, read from experiments/runner_xdomain.py module constants at build time. Every budget and decoding knob is IDENTICAL to v1.0.0's run_config.json; what differs is the benchmark/slice/domain and the domain-adapted Arm A + evaluator prompts.

arm_contract_differs_by_domain.WARNING: ARM A IS NOT THE SAME CONTRACT IN THE TWO DOMAINS. Do not assume one contract across the release.
arm_contract_differs_by_domain.arm_A: DOMAIN-ADAPTED (option b). 4 of 6 Arm A strings differ from v1.0.0.
arm_contract_differs_by_domain.arm_B: BYTE-IDENTICAL to v1.0.0 (asserted in code at build time).
arm_contract_differs_by_domain.consequence: P1a and every clause-specific role-fidelity metric are NOT transported across domains and were deliberately not computed: scoring SciBench agents against Omni-MATH clauses would score them against instructions they never received.
arm_contract_differs_by_domain.evaluator: DOMAIN-ADAPTED for units / significant figures / scientific notation. COMMON MODE: byte-identical across arms A and B within this domain, so it cannot manufacture an A-vs-B difference; it sets the difficulty floor only.
arm_contract_differs_by_domain.why_adapt_rather_than_reuse: Arm B's generic prompt contains no domain language, so leaving Arm A's math-specific wording in place would make the two arms differ in TWO ways -- role structure AND domain fit -- and the domain-fit difference runs against Arm A. Adapting A restores a single-variable manipulation. Every structural clause of A is preserved (role separation, DELTA, required structure, Diagnosis/Fix Instruction, answer ownership, routing tags); only domain nouns and the answer-form enumeration change.

arms_not_run.C: not run in this domain -- no enforcement_events table exists for SciBench

config_version.KNOWN LIMITATION -- config_version does: Same limitation as v1.0.0: config_version_hash() does not hash the logging code, so it cannot distinguish instrumented from uninstrumented rows. Use chars_per_sec, not config_version, to detect F13.
config_version.verification: Recomputed config_version_hash() from experiments/runner_xdomain.py and reproduced aed89f28ab338bdb exactly, matching the value stamped on all 2,296 frozen rows.
config_version.why_it_differs_from_the_omnimath_hashes: The hash covers every prompt string plus benchmark_id and slice_id. Arm A and the evaluator were domain-adapted and the benchmark changed, so the hash necessarily differs. It is NOT poolable with the Omni-MATH hashes, and that is the point of the field.
